question.value: What are the properties of multiple-scale molecular structures (clumps and clouds) in the dwarf galaxy NGC 404, and how are their properties and gas turbulence regulated by clump-clump collisions?

evidence.quote: We present a study of molecular structures (clumps and clouds) in the dwarf galaxy NGC 404 using high-resolution ($\approx0.86\times0.51$ pc$^2$) Atacama Large Millimeter/sub-millimeter Array $^{12}$CO(2-1) observations.

In this paper, we perform statistical analyses of the multiple-scale molecular structures of the dwarf lenticular galaxy NGC 404, exploiting high-spatial resolution ($\approx0.86\times0.51$ pc$^2$) Atacama Large Millimeter/sub-millimeter Array (ALMA) $^{12}$CO(2-1) observations.
The data underlying this article are available in the ALMA archive (https://almascience.eso.org/asax/) under project code: (i) 2015.1.00597.S, (ii) 2017.1.00572.S and (iii) 2017.1.00907.S.

analysis_steps.goal: Fit clump mass distribution functions, size-linewidth relations, mass-size relations, and virial parameters across galactic regions

method.value: Divide structures into central region (R_gal <= 15 pc) and molecular ring (15 < R_gal <= 50 pc); fit broken power-laws to differential mass functions, power-laws to cumulative mass functions, size-linewidth, mass-size, and virial parameter-mass relations; compute virial parameters and self-gravitating gas fractions

evidence.quote: Hereafter we will refer to the central disc/ring and arm-like feature as the central region (galactocentric distances $R_{\rm gal}\le15$ pc), and to the outer incomplete (pseudo-)ring as the molecular ring ($15<R_{\rm gal}\lesssim50$ pc).

We therefore fit the normalised differential mass distributions with two separate power-laws, one for the high-mass regime $M_{\rm clump}\gtrsim4000$ M$_\odot$, with a power-law index of $\gamma_{\rm clump}^+$, and the other for the low-mass regime $M_{\rm comp}\lesssim M_{\rm clump}\lesssim4000$ M$_\odot$, with a power-law index of $\gamma_{\rm clump}^-$.

We also calculate the fraction of emission originating from gravitationally-bound (i.e. $\alpha_{\rm vir,c} \le \alpha_{\rm vir,crit}=2$) structures, and plot this fraction as a function of the structures’ spatial scales in Fig. 8.

findings_qualitative.value: NGC 404 has two distinct molecular gas regions: a gravitationally-stable central region (Q = 3-30) and a gravitationally-unstable molecular ring (Q <= 1 at R_gal >= 27 pc).

evidence.quote: We find two distinct regions in NGC 404: a gravitationally-stable central region (Toomre parameter $Q=3-30$) and a gravitationally-unstable molecular ring ($Q\lesssim1$).

findings_qualitative.value: In the molecular ring, clump-clump collisions driven by gravitational instabilities and galactic shear regulate clump masses, sizes, mass-size relation, and turbulence.

evidence.quote: Our model-predicted clump masses and sizes (and mass – size relation) and turbulence energy injection rates (and size – linewidth relation) match the observations in the molecular ring very well, suggesting clump-clump collisions is the main mechanism regulating clump properties and gas turbulence in that region.

findings_qualitative.value: Clumps in the molecular ring are supported by collision-induced turbulence in rough virial equilibrium, while clouds are dominated by self-gravity.

evidence.quote: Collision-induced turbulence can thus maintain the clumps (but not the clouds) in rough virial equilibria.

findings_qualitative.value: In the central region, the collision model does not apply, and high velocity dispersions and uniform clump properties are likely explained by inward clump migration from the molecular ring.

evidence.quote: As expected, our collision model does not apply to the central region, where turbulence is likely driven by clump migration.

claims.hypothesis: Clump-clump collisions driven by gravitational instabilities and galactic shear regulate clump masses, sizes, and gas turbulence in the gravitationally-unstable molecular ring of NGC 404.
claims.experiment: Construct an analytical clump-clump collision model with no free parameters and compare its predictions for clump mass, size, mass-size relation, energy injection rate, and size-linewidth relation to ASTRODENDRO/CPROPSTOO measurements in the molecular ring.
claims.result: Predicted M_c,coll (~4000 M_sun), R_c,coll, mass-size slope (5/3 vs observed 1.63 +/- 0.04), and size-linewidth relation (slope 1/3 and flattening at ~3 pc vs observed 0.30 +/- 0.03) match observations in the molecular ring (especially at R_gal >= 27 pc where Q <= 1).
claims.finding: Clump-clump collisions are the dominant mechanism regulating clump properties and gas turbulence in the molecular ring of NGC 404.

evidence.quote: Our model-predicted clump masses and sizes (and mass – size relation) and turbulence energy injection rates (and size – linewidth relation) match the observations in the molecular ring very well, suggesting clump-clump collisions is the main mechanism regulating clump properties and gas turbulence in that region.

evidence.loc: Size – linewidth relation regulated by clump-clump collisions
evidence.quote: Our predicted size – linewidth relation (with no free parameter!) strongly resembles the observed $R_{\rm c}$ – $\sigma_{\rm obs,los}$ trend in the molecular ring (see the middle panel of Fig. 4), including its slope, normalisation, turn-over scale and plateau.

claims.hypothesis: In the molecular ring, clumps and clouds have their density structures and dynamical states regulated by different physical mechanisms (turbulence vs self-gravity).
claims.experiment: Compare mass-size power-law indices (D_m) and mean virial parameters (<alpha_vir>) of dendrogram leaves (clumps) and branches/trunks (clouds) in the molecular ring against Jeans and Toomre mass scales.
claims.result: Clumps have D_m,clump = 1.63 +/- 0.04 and <alpha_vir,clump> = 1.82 +/- 0.07, whereas clouds have D_m,cloud = 2.06 +/- 0.01 and <alpha_vir,cloud> = 0.41 +/- 0.02.
claims.finding: Clumps have masses near the Jeans/collision critical mass and are supported in rough virial equilibrium by collision-induced turbulence, while clouds are more massive and dominated by self-gravity (except the most massive trunks which are dominated by shear).

evidence.quote: In the molecular ring, clumps exhibit a shallower mass – size relation and larger virial parameters than clouds, implying density structures and dynamics are regulated by different physical mechanisms at different spatial scales.

Molecular structures with masses $\approx M_{\rm c,coll}$ (or $\approx M_{\rm Jeans}$), that are typically clumps, have their internal structures and dynamics dominated by collision-induced turbulence (see Section 5.2.1), that is not only able to support them against gravity in a rough virial equilibrium, but also shapes them to yield a mass – size relation with a power-law index $D_{\rm m}$ smaller than $2$: $M_{\rm clump}\propto R_{\rm clump}^{5/3}$.

claims.hypothesis: Stellar feedback (supernovae) is a major driver of turbulence in NGC 404.
claims.experiment: Estimate upper limit on SFR density from high-sensitivity 33 GHz VLA radio continuum observations and compare the resulting supernova energy injection rate with clump energy dissipation and collision injection rates.
claims.result: Upper limit on supernova energy injection rate is <= 2.5 km^2 s^-2 Myr^-1, smaller than the observed clump dissipation and collision injection rates (~10 km^2 s^-2 Myr^-1).
claims.finding: Feedback-driven turbulence is much less important than collision-driven turbulence in NGC 404.

evidence.loc: Effect of stellar feedback on turbulence
evidence.quote: This upper limit to the energy injection rate (per unit mass) from stellar feedback is clearly smaller than the observed energy dissipation rate (per unit mass) of clumps and the energy injection rate (per unit mass) from clump-clump collisions, i.e. $\dot{\epsilon}_{\rm SN}<\dot{\epsilon}_{\rm diss,clump}\approx\dot{\epsilon}_{\rm inject,coll}\approx10$ km$^2$ s$^{-2}$ Myr$^{-1}$ (see panel (c) in Fig. 9).

evidence.loc: Effect of stellar feedback on turbulence
evidence.quote: It therefore seems that feedback-driven turbulence is much less important than collision-driven turbulence in NGC 404.

claims.hypothesis: Inward clump migration from the molecular ring explains why clumps in the gravitationally-stable central region have similar masses/sizes to those in the ring and drives the high central turbulence.
claims.experiment: Calculate the viscous migration timescale and migration energy injection rate at the boundary (R_0 = 15 pc) and compare with the central gas disc energy dissipation rate.
claims.result: Migration timescale is ~10 Myr (~5.6 t_orbit), and migration energy injection rate (~230 km^2 s^-2 Myr^-1) matches the central disc energy dissipation rate (~250 km^2 s^-2 Myr^-1), though direct kinematic inflow is not detected due to face-on orientation.
claims.finding: Clump migration likely explains the uniform clump properties and is a major driver of turbulence in the central region, though direct evidence is lacking and other mechanisms (e.g. jet-ISM interaction) may also contribute.

evidence.loc: Clump migration towards the galaxy centre
evidence.quote: Unfortunately, we have not found direct evidence of clump migration (i.e. inflow) in NGC 404, as its gas disc is viewed nearly face-on ($i\approx9.3\ensuremath{^\circ}$ at $R_{\rm gal}\ge15$ pc; (cite: davis2020)) and detecting clear non-circular motions is very difficult.

evidence.loc: Clump migration towards the galaxy centre
evidence.quote: It thus seems that clump migration may be the major mechanism driving turbulence in the central region of NGC 404, where the observed large velocity dispersions cannot be explained by clump-clump collisions or stellar feedback. However, other mechanisms may also play a role given the potential jet-ISM interaction in the core of this galaxy.

why_this_data.value: High-spatial resolution (~0.86 x 0.51 pc^2) ALMA CO(2-1) observations resolve sub-parsec to tens-of-parsec molecular structures across the dwarf galaxy disc, with maximum recoverable scale (~10.4'') much larger than the largest single molecular structure.

evidence.quote: In this paper, we perform statistical analyses of the multiple-scale molecular structures of the dwarf lenticular galaxy NGC 404, exploiting high-spatial resolution ($\approx0.86\times0.51$ pc$^2$) Atacama Large Millimeter/sub-millimeter Array (ALMA) $^{12}$CO(2-1) observations.
and a maximum recoverable scale of $\approx10.4\ensuremath{''}$ that is much larger than than the largest single molecular structure identified in this work.

why_this_method.value: ASTRODENDRO identifies a full hierarchy of nested structures (leaves, branches, trunks) to probe multiple spatial scales, while CPROPSTOO extrapolates to infinite S/N and deconvolves the beam to correct for finite sensitivity and resolution biases.

evidence.quote: As a dendrogram approach allows us to identify a full hierarchy of molecular structures, we are able to investigate whether the size – linewidth relation (and thus turbulence) is universal from the large-scale ISM to its smallest and densest structures (cite: shetty2012).

The code CPROPSTOO is chosen because it attempts to correct the measured quantities for the finite sensitivity of the observations, extrapolating sizes, linewidths and luminosities to their infinite signal-to-noise ratio ($S/N$) equivalents

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Using gradient-subtracted velocity dispersion (sigma_gs,los) instead of observed velocity dispersion (sigma_obs,los) was rejected as unnecessary because galactic rotation contamination is negligible at clump/cloud scales.

evidence.quote: Following the method of (cite: liu2021) (i.e. comparing $\sigma_{\rm obs,los}$ with the gradient-subtracted velocity dispersion measure $\sigma_{\rm gs,los}$), we found no evidence of a significant contribution of galactic rotation at the clump and cloud scales (i.e. $\sigma_{\rm obs,los}\approx\sigma_{\rm gs,los}$ for most clumps and clouds).
The use of the gradient-subtracted velocity dispersion $\sigma_{\rm gs,los}$ is therefore unnecessary in this work.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Cloud-cloud collisions were rejected as unimportant compared to clump-clump collisions because clouds have collision timescales longer than the shear timescale (t_coll,cloud > t_shear).

evidence.quote: Clouds, that by definition contains several clumps, should therefore have $t_{\rm coll,cloud}>t_{\rm shear}$ everywhere.
Cloud-cloud collisions are therefore likely to be much less important than clump-clump collisions in NGC 404.

limitations_admitted.value: Findings are based on only one galaxy; high-resolution observations of more gravitationally-unstable discs are needed to confirm the model.

evidence.quote: We note, however, that our findings are based on only one galaxy. High-resolution observations of molecular gas in more gravitationally-unstable gas discs are thus needed to further confirm our model.

limitations_admitted.value: Direct kinematic evidence of inward clump migration is not detected because the gas disc is viewed nearly face-on.

evidence.loc: Clump migration towards the galaxy centre
evidence.quote: Unfortunately, we have not found direct evidence of clump migration (i.e. inflow) in NGC 404, as its gas disc is viewed nearly face-on ($i\approx9.3\ensuremath{^\circ}$ at $R_{\rm gal}\ge15$ pc; (cite: davis2020)) and detecting clear non-circular motions is very difficult.

limitations_admitted.value: Distance uncertainty to NGC 404 is not propagated into the tabulated uncertainties of measured structure properties.

evidence.quote: The uncertainty of the adopted distance $D$ to NGC 404 was not propagated through the tabulated uncertainties of the measured quantities.

referee_caveats_inferred: Adoption of a constant standard Galactic X_CO conversion factor and a single uniform CO(2-1)/CO(1-0) ratio across both the LINER central region and the outer molecular ring may bias mass and virial parameter estimates.

Deprojecting R_gal and computing radial profiles with a fixed PA = 1 deg and inclination i = 9.3 deg across all radii ignores the strongly warped inner disc orientation (i = 37.1 deg, PA = 37.2 deg within R_gal <= 8 pc).
